title: $Lf^*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of the
setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$ is bounded constructible
([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $Lf^*K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$
([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]).

proof.text: First verify exactness for every commutative condensed ring, not just the admissible adic rings. On abelian sheaves the tensor product is closed symmetric monoidal and tensoring preserves colimits, hence is additive and right exact [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Thus the module categories in question are abelian [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian]. The inverse image $f^*_{\Ab}$ is exact [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]. The functor $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ commutes with the forgetful functors by [def-sfb-modobj-transport]; apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] to conclude it is additive and exact. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $\alpha_f$ is invertible for this arbitrary $\Lambda$. Extension along it is naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}$ [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso]. Restriction is the identity on underlying objects and morphisms [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], so the same lifted-exactness lemma, now with underlying functor the identity of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, proves this restriction exact. Consequently the composite $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] is additive and exact. This argument applies to every morphism of schemes, including the maps between strata and covers used below.

source.place: First sentence: exactness of the module-object pullback; expand its two factors

proof.text:
Represent $K$ by a complex $C$ and take a K-flat resolution $P\to C$. By the definition of the total derived composite [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $Lf^*K$ is represented by $f^*P$. The exact-functor cohomology isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], applied to the exact functor of step 1, gives
$$H^q(Lf^*K)=H^q(f^*P)\simeq f^*H^q(P)\simeq f^*H^q(K).$$
The last isomorphism is induced by the quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$. Choose a finite interval $[a,b]$ outside which $H^q(K)=0$, as in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. An additive functor sends the zero object to a zero object, so the displayed formula gives $H^q(Lf^*K)=0$ outside the same interval. It remains to check constructibility of $f^*M$ for any constructible module $M$.

source.place: First two sentences: termwise computation, cohomology, and boundedness

proof.text: Choose a witnessing finite stratification $(i_a:Y_a\hookrightarrow Y)_a$ and pro-étale covers $u_{ai}:U_{ai}\to Y_a$ for the finite constant local models in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Put $X_a=X\times_Y Y_a$, with maps $j_a:X_a\to X$ and $f_a:X_a\to Y_a$. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] these maps give a finite stratification of $X$ with images $f^{-1}(|Y_a|)$. The schemes $X,Y$ are of finite type over the field $k$ by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. In particular their topological spaces are Noetherian, and their locally closed strata are constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Thus this is a stratification of the kind required by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], including its constructible-subset condition. Empty strata may be removed; no reduced scheme structure or equality of scheme-theoretic fibres with set-theoretic preimages is assumed.

source.place: Stratification and its inverse image; retain constructibility of the strata

proof.text: For each $a$, form $V_{ai}=X_a\times_{Y_a}U_{ai}$, with projections $v_{ai}:V_{ai}\to X_a$ and $h_{ai}:V_{ai}\to U_{ai}$. The arrows $u_{ai}$ are weakly étale and the family is fpqc, by the covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]. Base change preserves weak étaleness [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] and preserves fpqc covering families [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Hence $(v_{ai})_i$ is again a pro-étale cover of $X_a$. These results impose no Noetherian, finite-type, surjectivity-of-each-arrow, or quasi-compactness-of-each-arrow assumption, so they apply to the chosen cover.

Pullback composition [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] gives the required comparison on this cover. Indeed $f j_a=i_a f_a$ and $f_a v_{ai}=u_{ai}h_{ai}$, and therefore
$$v_{ai}^*j_a^*f^*M\simeq v_{ai}^*f_a^*i_a^*M\simeq h_{ai}^*u_{ai}^*i_a^*M.$$
Thus it suffices to pull back the finite scalar-matrix presentation of $u_{ai}^*i_a^*M$ along $h_{ai}$. This uses composition of module-object pullbacks, rather than an underived base-change assertion about pushforwards.

source.place: The restriction identity obtained by composition of pullbacks

proof.text:
Write the local model as the cokernel of a finite matrix $A_{ai}$ with entries in $R=\Lambda(*)$:
$$u_{ai}^*i_a^*M\simeq\operatorname{coker}(A_{ai}:\Lambda_{U_{ai}}^{m_{ai}}\to\Lambda_{U_{ai}}^{n_{ai}}),$$
as permitted by the scalar-matrix formulation of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. From the formula in [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and the transport action in [def-sfb-modobj-transport], pullback sends the regular module $\Lambda_U$ to the regular module $\Lambda_V$: its first factor sends $\Lambda_U$ to the regular $h^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_U$-module, and extension of scalars identifies the latter with $\Lambda_V$ by the map $b\otimes a\mapsto b\alpha_h(a)$. Its inverse is $b\mapsto b\otimes1$: the unit gives one composite equal to the identity, and the balancing relation $b\alpha_h(a)\otimes1=b\otimes a$ gives the other. These formulas denote the maps induced by multiplication and unit on the relative tensor product. Additivity from step 1 sends its finite direct sums to the same finite direct sums. Moreover a scalar $r\in\Lambda(*)$ gives a morphism $r:\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ of condensed abelian groups. Put $r_U=p_U^*r:\mathbf1_U\to\Lambda_U$ and $r_V=p_V^*r:\mathbf1_V\to\Lambda_V$; its action is $\mu_U(r_U\otimes\mathrm{id})$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $\beta:h^*_{\Ab}p_U^*\xrightarrow{\sim}p_V^*$ be the monoidal natural isomorphism of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. Its component $\beta_\Lambda$ is $\alpha_h$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and naturality at the abelian-group morphism $r$ gives $\alpha_h\circ h^*_{\Ab}(r_U)=r_V\circ\beta_{\mathbf Z}$. Monoidality identifies $\beta_{\mathbf Z}$ with the unit comparison and identifies the transported multiplication with that of $\Lambda_V$. Consequently the pulled-back action $\mu_U(r_U\otimes\mathrm{id})$, under the regular-module identification just written, is $\mu_V(r_V\otimes\mathrm{id})$. This uses naturality on abelian sheaves; $r$ is not required to be a morphism of rings. Thus the pulled-back matrix is exactly $A_{ai}$ with the same scalar entries, not an arbitrary matrix over sections on $V_{ai}$. Right exactness from step 1 now gives
$$h_{ai}^*(u_{ai}^*i_a^*M)\simeq\operatorname{coker}(A_{ai}:\Lambda_{V_{ai}}^{m_{ai}}\to\Lambda_{V_{ai}}^{n_{ai}}).$$
The ranks are finite and may be zero. Together with step 5 this is a finite constant local model for $(f^*M)|_{X_a}$ on the cover of step 4.

source.place: Last sentences: finite free modules, right exactness, and the scalar entries of the presentations

proof.text: Steps 3–6 give the witnessing finite constructible stratification and finite constant local models for $f^*M$; hence $f^*M$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Apply this to every $M=H^q(K)$. The isomorphisms of step 2 show that all $H^q(Lf^*K)$ are constructible, and step 2 already supplies the finite cohomological interval. These are precisely the two conditions of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Therefore $Lf^*K$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Conclusion: boundedness and constructibility of every cohomology sheaf
